signs.name: Stop
signs.meaning: Come to a complete stop. Wait until safe, then go.
signs.analogy: Like a teacher holding up a STOP hand — freeze completely.

signs.name: Give Way (Yield)
signs.meaning: Slow down. Let other traffic go first, then join when safe.
signs.analogy: Like holding a door open — let others pass before you.

signs.name: No Entry
signs.meaning: You may not enter this road from your direction.
signs.analogy: Red circle with bar = 'road closed to you'.

signs.name: Mandatory: Turn Left
signs.meaning: You MUST turn left here. No other choice.
signs.analogy: Blue circle = you have to do this.

signs.name: Mandatory: Keep Left
signs.meaning: Stay on the left side of the divider.
signs.analogy: Blue circle = a rule you must follow.

signs.name: Minimum Speed 60
signs.meaning: You MUST drive at least 60 km/h in this lane — no slower.
signs.analogy: Blue circle with number = a floor, not a ceiling.

signs.name: Headlights On
signs.meaning: Switch your headlights on (dipped) — you must be seen.
signs.analogy: Blue circle + lamp = lights compulsory.

signs.name: Speed Limit 60
signs.meaning: Do NOT go faster than 60 km/h. Maximum, not a target.
signs.analogy: Red circle = a strict ceiling, like a toy car's speed cap.

signs.name: No Overtaking
signs.meaning: Do NOT overtake other vehicles on this stretch of road.
signs.analogy: Two cars with a red slash = no passing.

signs.name: No U-Turn
signs.meaning: You may NOT turn around here.
signs.analogy: U-arrow crossed out = no going back.

signs.name: No Left Turn
signs.meaning: You may NOT turn left at this point.
signs.analogy: Arrow left with red slash = no left turn.

signs.name: No Right Turn
signs.meaning: You may NOT turn right at this point.
signs.analogy: Arrow right with red slash = no right turn.

signs.name: No Parking
signs.meaning: You may NOT park here at any time.
signs.analogy: Red circle, P crossed out = no parking.

signs.name: No Stopping
signs.meaning: You may NOT stop here at all — not even to drop someone off.
signs.analogy: Red circle, X = absolute no stopping.

signs.name: Warning: Children
signs.meaning: Children may be near the road. Slow down and watch out.
signs.analogy: Yellow triangle = caution, like a wet-floor sign.

signs.name: Warning: Curve Ahead
signs.meaning: The road bends ahead. Slow before the curve.
signs.analogy: Triangle points the danger — bend coming, ease off gas.

signs.name: Warning: Pedestrian Crossing
signs.meaning: People may walk across. Stop for them.
signs.analogy: Zebra stripes on road = people first, always.

signs.name: Warning: Animals
signs.meaning: Farm animals may be on the road. Drive slowly.
signs.analogy: Triangle = something unexpected ahead.

signs.name: Warning: Steep Hill
signs.meaning: Steep uphill or downhill ahead. Use a lower gear.
signs.analogy: Triangle = road shape changes sharply.

signs.name: Warning: Slippery Road
signs.meaning: The road may be slippery, especially when wet. Slow down.
signs.analogy: Triangle = surface grip drops — ease off.

signs.name: Warning: Speed Bump
signs.meaning: A bump is ahead. Slow right down.
signs.analogy: Triangle = bump — drop your speed.

signs.name: Warning: Railway Crossing
signs.meaning: Railway tracks ahead. Stop if a train is coming. Never race a train.
signs.analogy: X = tracks cross the road.

signs.name: Warning: Road Narrows
signs.meaning: The road narrows ahead. Keep well to the left.
signs.analogy: Triangle = space shrinks — ease off.

signs.name: Right of Way (Priority)
signs.meaning: Traffic on your road has priority over the road ahead of you.
signs.analogy: Thick arrow up = you go first.

signs.name: Warning: Crossroads Ahead
signs.meaning: A four-way crossing is ahead. Slow down and look both ways.
signs.analogy: Triangle = junction — be ready to yield.

signs.name: Warning: T-Junction Ahead
signs.meaning: The road ends at a T. You must turn left or right.
signs.analogy: Triangle = junction shape changes.

signs.name: Warning: Y-Junction Ahead
signs.meaning: The road splits into a Y ahead. Slow and choose your fork.
signs.analogy: Triangle = road splits.

signs.name: Warning: Roundabout Ahead
signs.meaning: A roundabout is coming up. Slow down and be ready to yield to the right.
signs.analogy: Circle with arrows = go around, yield right.

signs.name: Warning: School Zone
signs.meaning: Children are around. Slow right down — to 40 km/h if a sign shows it — especially at school times.
signs.analogy: Children near a road = extra caution.

signs.name: Warning: Pedestrian Crossing
signs.meaning: A marked crossing is ahead. Slow down — pedestrians have priority.
signs.analogy: People stripes = be ready to stop.

signs.name: Warning: Cyclists
signs.meaning: Cyclists may be on the road ahead. Give them space.
signs.analogy: Triangle = two wheels ahead.

signs.name: Warning: Wild Animals
signs.meaning: Wild animals may cross the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.
signs.analogy: Triangle = unexpected on the road.

signs.name: Info: Hospital
signs.meaning: A hospital is ahead or nearby.
signs.analogy: Green box = helpful info, like a map pin.

signs.name: Info: Parking
signs.meaning: A place to park is available here.
signs.analogy: Blue box = here is something useful.

signs.name: Info: Toll Road
signs.meaning: A toll road ahead. A free alternative route may be shown.
signs.analogy: Blue box with R = pay route, alt shown.

signs.name: Info: Direction
signs.meaning: Shows the direction and distance to a place or route.
signs.analogy: Blue box with arrow = follow this way.

signs.name: Pedestrian Signal: Red Man
signs.meaning: Pedestrians must NOT start crossing. Wait.
signs.analogy: Red man = stop, do not walk.

signs.name: Pedestrian Signal: Green Man
signs.meaning: Pedestrians may cross carefully within the markings.
signs.analogy: Green man = walk when safe.

rules.q: Which side of the road do we drive on in South Africa?
rules.a: The LEFT. Pass other cars on their right. 'Keep left, pass right.'
w: The RIGHT. Pass other cars on their left.
Stick to the middle unless overtaking.
Whichever lane is fastest.

rules.q: No signs or robots (traffic lights) at a crossing — who goes first?
rules.a: The car coming from your RIGHT. Simple: 'right goes first.'
w: The car coming from your LEFT goes first.
The larger vehicle goes first.
Traffic on the main road always goes first.

rules.q: Town/city speed limit?
rules.a: 60 km/h — unless a sign says otherwise.
w: 80 km/h — unless a sign says otherwise.
100 km/h — unless a sign says otherwise.
40 km/h — unless a sign says otherwise.

rules.q: Rural road speed limit (outside town, not a freeway)?
rules.a: 100 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
w: 120 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
80 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
60 km/h on all country roads.

rules.q: National highway (freeway) speed limit?
rules.a: 120 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
w: 100 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
140 km/h — unless a sign shows lower.
80 km/h on all freeways.

rules.q: Robot turns yellow. What do you do?
rules.a: Stop if you can do so safely. Too close to stop? Continue carefully.
w: Always stop sharply before the line.
Speed up to beat the red light.
Ignore it — yellow is just a warning.

rules.q: How far behind the car ahead?
rules.a: At least 2 seconds (3 in rain). Count 'one-thousand-two'.
w: At least 1 second (count one-thousand-one).
At least 3 seconds at all times.
About half a car length at town speed.

rules.q: Who must wear a seatbelt?
rules.a: Driver AND all passengers, front and back. Every trip.
w: Only the driver and front passenger.
Only the driver when on a freeway.
Adults only, not children in the back.

rules.q: At a roundabout you must...
rules.a: Go clockwise. Yield to traffic already on it — approaching from your RIGHT.
w: Go anti-clockwise. Yield to traffic on your left.
Stop and wait for someone to wave you in.
Go straight through and flash your lights.

rules.q: Blood alcohol for a LEARNER?
rules.a: Effectively zero. The legal limit for learners is 0.02 g per 100 ml — so no alcohol at all.
w: 0.05 g per 100 ml — same as a normal driver.
0.02 g per 100 ml — a small drink is allowed.
No limit while you are only practising.

rules.q: Pedestrians crossing at a marked crossing?
rules.a: Stop and let them cross. People first.
w: Only stop the first car, others may continue.
Honk so they move faster.
Stop only if the pedestrians are on your side.

rules.q: How close to an intersection may you park (in town)?
rules.a: Not within 5 metres of the corner — and never on or across a pedestrian crossing.
w: Within 5 metres of the corner if it is a weekday.
Not within 10 metres of the corner.
Right on the corner, but only after dark.

rules.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?
rules.a: Not within 1.5 metres — the fire service needs clear access.
w: Not within 5 metres of the hydrant.
Right next to it, as long as the cap is clear.
Within 1 metre, but only in an emergency.

rules.q: What does a YELLOW kerb line mean?
rules.a: No parking at any time. A RED kerb line means no stopping at all.
w: No stopping at any time.
Loading and unloading allowed.
No parking during school hours only.

rules.q: How do you overtake another vehicle?
rules.a: Only on the RIGHT, when the road is clear and the centre line is broken on your side — never on a solid barrier line.
w: On the LEFT, when the road is clear.
On the RIGHT, even over a solid centre line.
On either side, whichever is shorter.

rules.q: What must you NOT do when another car is overtaking you?
rules.a: Speed up or block them. Keep left, slow down if needed, and let them pass safely.
w: Slow down to help them pass.
Signal to the right to let them know.
Pull off the road completely.

rules.q: When must you switch on your headlights?
rules.a: From sunset to sunrise, when you cannot see 150 m ahead, and when it rains and you cannot see 100 m ahead.
w: Only between sunset and sunrise.
Only when it is raining.
Only when another car has its lights on.

rules.q: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren approaches. What do you do?
rules.a: Slow down, pull over safely to the left, and stop until it has passed. Give it right of way.
w: Speed up to get out of its way.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Continue and let it pass on the left.

rules.q: When may you use the hooter (horn)?
rules.a: Only to warn other road users of danger — not to greet, hurry, or show frustration.
w: To greet a friend you recognise.
To hurry a slow driver ahead.
To signal that you are turning.

rules.q: On a hill, which way do you turn your front wheels when parking?
rules.a: Toward the kerb when facing downhill, away from the kerb when facing uphill — so the car cannot roll into traffic.
w: Toward the kerb when facing uphill.
Toward the kerb in both directions.
Away from the kerb when facing downhill.

rules.q: When the vehicle is stationary, what must you do?
rules.a: Apply the parking brake and select neutral (or Park) so it cannot roll — especially on a gradient.
w: Leave it in gear with the engine on.
Apply the parking brake and leave it in gear only.
Rely on the foot brake to hold it.

rules.q: While the vehicle is moving, may you hold a cell phone?
rules.a: NO. Holding a phone is illegal. Use hands-free only. Learners: no phone at all while driving.
w: Only if you use a hands-free headset.
Yes, if you keep one hand on the wheel.
Only when stopped at a red light.

rules.q: When refuelling (petrol/diesel), what must you do?
rules.a: Switch the engine OFF. Never leave it running while fuel is being transferred.
w: Leave the engine running to keep the pump working.
Switch it off only for petrol, not diesel.
Keep the engine idling so the tank fills faster.

rules.q: Trailers under 10 000 kg GVM — what reflective material is needed?
rules.a: Yellow reflective material on the SIDES and the REAR of the trailer.
w: Red reflective material on the front only.
Yellow reflective material on the FRONT of the trailer.
White reflective material on the sides.

rules.q: When must projection flags be used and what size?
rules.a: Red flags, at least 300 mm × 300 mm, to mark loads that stick out.
w: Blue flags, at least 200 mm × 200 mm.
Red flags of any size.
Yellow flags, at least 300 mm × 300 mm.

rules.q: Are pedal cycles allowed on a freeway?
rules.a: Generally NO. Pedestrians, animals, and pedal cycles are not allowed on freeways.
w: Yes, if riding on the shoulder.
Yes, during daylight hours.
Yes, if they use the left lane.

rules.q: What is the minimum following distance in adverse conditions?
rules.a: Increase it — 3 seconds in rain, more for heavy vehicles or at speed.
w: Keep the normal 2-second distance.
Reduce it to 1 second in rain.
Only increase it for heavy vehicles.

rules.q: When may you stop on a freeway?
rules.a: Only in an emergency or a designated stopping area. Never just to look at the view.
w: To answer a phone call.
To check a map or directions.
Any time there is a wide shoulder.

rules.q: If your vehicle breaks down, where do you place the warning triangle?
rules.a: At least 45 m behind the vehicle, on the roadside.
w: At least 15 m behind, close to the vehicle.
In front of the vehicle, facing oncoming.
On the roof of the vehicle.

rules.q: What is the minimum tyre tread depth?
rules.a: At least 1 mm across the full width and circumference of the tyre.
w: At least 1.6 mm across the tread.
At least 3 mm for safety.
No legal minimum — judge by wear bars.

rules.q: May you use hand signals on a freeway?
rules.a: NO. Hand signals are not allowed on freeways except in an emergency.
w: Yes, always use them when turning.
Only at night when lights are bright.
Yes, if the indicator is broken.

rules.q: What is the rule for convoys over long weekends?
rules.a: Vehicles may NOT travel in convoy over long weekends/public holidays (6pm before to 6am after).
w: Convoys are allowed if under 10 vehicles.
Only government vehicles may convoy.
Convoys are allowed during the day only.

rules.q: When towing another vehicle, what must you keep?
rules.a: A safe following distance and the tow connection secure; indicator hand signals if needed.
w: A speed of at least 80 km/h.
The tow rope taut at all times.
Your headlights on dipped beam.

rules.q: Learner drivers on a freeway — allowed?
rules.a: YES, if accompanied by a properly licensed driver. But not at night unless permitted.
w: No, never on a freeway.
Yes, if driving at night with a licensed driver.
Yes, but only in the right lane.

rules.q: When may you NOT overtake because of limited visibility?
rules.a: Never overtake where you cannot see at least 150 m ahead — on a hill crest, a curve, or any restricted view.
w: Never overtake where you cannot see at least 100 m ahead.
Only stop overtaking after dark.
Never overtake on a straight road.

rules.q: How far may the tow-line be when towing another vehicle?
rules.a: No more than 3.5 m between the vehicles. Keep it shorter than that.
w: No more than 5 m between the vehicles.
As long as it is visible and flagged.
No more than 2 m between the vehicles.

rules.q: May passengers ride in a vehicle that is being towed?
rules.a: NO. Passengers are not allowed in a towed vehicle on a public road.
w: Yes, if the vehicle has working brakes.
Yes, if the tow speed is under 20 km/h.
Only one passenger is allowed.

rules.q: How close to a marked pedestrian crossing may you stop or park?
rules.a: Not within 9 m of the approaching side of a marked pedestrian crossing.
w: Not within 5 m of the crossing.
Not within 15 m of the crossing.
Any distance, as long as you are not on the stripes.

rules.q: How close to a bridge, tunnel or subway may you stop?
rules.a: Not within 6 m — keep access clear for that structure.
w: Not within 3 m of the structure.
Not within 10 m of the structure.
Allowed if you leave your hazards on.

rules.q: How far must your dipped (low) beam light the road ahead?
rules.a: At least 45 m. Your main (high) beam must illuminate at least 100 m ahead.
w: At least 100 m ahead.
At least 30 m ahead.
Exactly the length of your car.

rules.q: South Africa is a RIGHT-hand-drive country. What does that mean?
rules.a: The driver sits on the RIGHT side, the steering wheel is on the right, and the gear lever is to the LEFT of the driver. We drive on the LEFT side of the road.
w: The driver sits on the LEFT and drives on the RIGHT.
The gear lever is to the RIGHT of the driver.
We drive on the RIGHT side of the road.

rules.q: After you have overtaken a vehicle on the right, what must you do?
rules.a: Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, then move back to the left lane as soon as it is safe. The right lane is for overtaking, not cruising.
w: Stay in the right lane for a few kilometres.
Move back right if traffic is slow.
Immediately brake to avoid the vehicle.

rules.q: When may you use the RIGHT lane on a highway?
rules.a: Only for overtaking, turning right, or avoiding an obstruction — then move back left. The right lane is not a cruising lane.
w: For steady cruising at highway speed.
Whenever the left lane feels crowded.
To pass slower vehicles and then too slow ones.

rules.q: What is the minimum speed on a freeway (unless a sign says otherwise)?
rules.a: 60 km/h. Do not drive slower than this without a good reason.
w: 120 km/h unless a sign says otherwise.
40 km/h unless a sign says otherwise.
No minimum — drive at whatever speed.

rules.q: You break down on a freeway. What must you do?
rules.a: Pull as far left as possible and switch on your hazard lights. Place the warning triangle 45 m behind. All passengers exit and stand BEHIND the barrier, away from traffic. Call 10177 or roadside assistance — never repair the vehicle in the lane.
w: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Push the vehicle to the right lane.
Ignore the hazard lights to save the battery.

rules.q: SA emergency number for a breakdown on the road?
rules.a: 10177 is the emergency services number; roadside assistance is also an option. Do not attempt repairs in a live lane.
w: 112 is the only number to call.
10111 is the emergency number.
911 is the SA emergency number.

controls.q: Which foot controls the CLUTCH (manual car)?
controls.ex: Left foot only for clutch. Right foot does brake + accelerator.

controls.q: Which pedal makes the car go faster?
Where should hands be on the wheel?
controls.ex: Hold at '10 and 2' — balanced and in control.

opts: To keep the car still when parked
controls.ex: Pull it when parked so the car cannot roll.

controls.q: Before moving off you must FIRST...
controls.ex: Look in mirrors, check blind spot, signal — then go.

controls.q: Which pedal is used to slow the car?
controls.ex: The foot brake slows the vehicle in normal driving.

controls.q: What is the STEERING WHEEL for?
controls.ex: Steering wheel turns the vehicle and changes direction.

controls.q: When may you adjust the mirrors?
opts: Only when the vehicle is stationary
controls.ex: Mirrors may only be adjusted when the vehicle is stationary.
Hooter = warn other road users of danger, nothing else.
Speedometer shows how fast you are travelling right now.

controls.q: To keep a parked vehicle from rolling you must...
controls.ex: Parking brake + neutral (or Park) locks it in place.

mock_extra.q: At a STOP sign you must...
opts: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe
Only stop if traffic is coming
Stop only if a police car is there
mock_extra.ex: Stop completely. Go only when it is safe.

mock_extra.q: A robot (traffic light) shows RED. You must...
mock_extra.ex: Stop before the line and wait for green.

mock_extra.q: An emergency vehicle with a siren is behind you. You should...
opts: Stop in the middle of the road
Pull over and let it pass
mock_extra.ex: Pull over safely and let it through.

mock_extra.q: At night you should use your headlights...
opts: From sunset to sunrise and when visibility is poor
mock_extra.ex: Keep your lights on whenever it is dark or hard to see.

mock_extra.q: You may cross a SOLID white line to overtake...
opts: If the car ahead is slow
mock_extra.ex: Solid white line = stay in your lane.

mock_extra.q: Before turning or changing lanes you must always...
opts: Check mirrors, signal, and look for other traffic
mock_extra.ex: Mirrors, signal, check blind spot — then move.

mock_extra.q: When refuelling, the engine must be...
mock_extra.ex: Switch the engine OFF while transferring fuel.

mock_extra.q: A cell phone while driving — what is the rule?
opts: Hold it if one hand on wheel
mock_extra.ex: Holding a phone is illegal. Hands-free only.

mock_extra.q: Pedestrian signal: red man showing. You must...
opts: Cross quickly if it is clear
Step out and wave traffic to stop
mock_extra.ex: Red man = pedestrians must not cross.

mock_extra.q: Minimum speed sign (blue circle, number). You must...
mock_extra.ex: Blue circle with number = minimum speed, a floor.

mock_extra.q: When two vehicles reach a 4-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
mock_extra.ex: At a simultaneous 4-way stop, the vehicle on your right goes first.

mock_extra.q: What is the legal blood-alcohol limit for an ORDINARY (private) driver?
mock_extra.ex: Ordinary drivers: 0.05 g/100 ml. Professional/learner: 0.02 g/100 ml.

mock_extra.q: No-overtaking signs apart — when else may you never overtake?
opts: At or near a pedestrian crossing
mock_extra.ex: Never overtake at/near a pedestrian crossing, intersection, tunnel or level crossing.

mock_extra.q: When approaching a LEFT-hand curve, you should...
opts: Slow down before the curve and stay in your lane
Keep the same speed and drift wide
mock_extra.ex: Slow down before a curve and hold your lane; do not brake sharply while turning.

mock_extra.q: What does a BROKEN (dashed) white centre line allow?
opts: Crossing to overtake only when safe
Driving on the wrong side freely
mock_extra.ex: A broken white line may be crossed to overtake when the road is clear and safe.

mock_extra.q: You are overtaking a bicycle in a 60 km/h zone. What is the minimum safe passing gap?
opts: You may crowd it if it is slow
mock_extra.ex: Leave at least 1 m between your car and a cyclist when passing.

mock_extra.q: A vehicle is indicating to turn RIGHT at an intersection. You are behind it. You may...
mock_extra.ex: You may pass a right-turning vehicle on its left only when safe.

mock_extra.q: What is the minimum age to get a Code 2 (light-vehicle) learner's licence?
mock_extra.ex: You must be 17 or older to apply for a Code 2 light-vehicle learner's licence.

mock_extra.q: The maximum mass of an unbraked trailer you may tow on a Code B (GVM 3 500 kg)?
mock_extra.ex: Code B normally allows an unbraked trailer up to 750 kg.

mock_extra.q: When is double-parking (stopping alongside a parked vehicle) allowed?
opts: When you are in a hurry
mock_extra.ex: Double-parking is never allowed on a public road.

mock_extra.q: What should you do at a STOP sign if the road is clear?
opts: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe
mock_extra.ex: A STOP sign requires a complete stop behind the line, then proceed when safe.

mock_extra.q: When may you use your high-beam (bright) headlights?
opts: On unlit roads where you will not dazzle oncoming traffic
mock_extra.ex: Use brights only on unlit roads where they will not dazzle oncoming drivers.

mock_extra.q: What does a flashing RED traffic light mean?
opts: Treat it as a STOP sign — stop then proceed when safe
mock_extra.ex: A flashing red light is a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe.

mock_extra.q: What does a flashing YELLOW/AMBER traffic light mean?
opts: Proceed with caution — yield to traffic
Treat it as a red light
mock_extra.ex: A flashing amber light means proceed with caution and yield.

mock_extra.q: A school-zone sign shows 40 km/h. This limit applies...
opts: When children are present or during school hours
mock_extra.ex: The 40 km/h school-zone limit applies when children are present/school hours.

mock_extra.q: Where must you position the wheels when parking uphill with a kerb?
opts: Front wheels turned away from the kerb
Front wheels turned toward the kerb
On the wrong side of the road
mock_extra.ex: Uphill: turn front wheels away from the kerb. Downhill: toward the kerb.

mock_extra.q: An ambulance with no lights or siren approaching. What do you do?
opts: Continue normally — pull over only when lights/siren are active
Move into the oncoming lane to pass
Stop in the middle of the road
mock_extra.ex: You only pull over for an emergency vehicle with lights and siren active.

mock_extra.q: An oncoming car's high beams dazzle you at night. What should you do?
opts: Look to the left edge of the road and slow down
Speed up to get past quickly
mock_extra.ex: Look to the left edge of your lane and slow down — never stare at oncoming brights.

mock_extra.q: Pedestrians waiting at a pedestrian crossing. The law says...
opts: Vehicles may continue if there is no robot
Vehicles may continue if pedestrians are on the far side
Vehicles must stop to let them cross
Only the first lane must stop
mock_extra.ex: Marked crossings give pedestrians priority; vehicles must stop for them.

mock_extra.q: What is the minimum clear space to keep from a bus loading/unloading passengers?
opts: You may stop right behind it
mock_extra.ex: Give buses loading/unloading at least 1 m clear space.

markings.t: Solid white line down the middle
markings.d: Stay in your lane. Do NOT cross to overtake.
markings.tip: Solid = stay put, like a wall.

markings.d: You MAY cross to pass, but only when safe.
No stopping at all — not even to drop someone off.
Pedestrian crossing — stop for people walking.
You may NOT drive on or over it. Go around it.
Do NOT stop in it unless your exit is clear.
Only that class of vehicle may drive or stop there.
No stopping at any time — emergency only.
No parking during the times shown on the plate.

row.scene: 4-way stop — you arrive at the same time as the car on your RIGHT.
opts: You go first — you were there first
The car on your RIGHT goes first
row.ex: At a 4-way stop, if two cars arrive together, the car on the right goes first.

row.scene: Roundabout — you are entering, a car is already on the circle to your right.
opts: Enter fast — you have right of way
Yield and let the car on the circle go first
row.ex: Yield to traffic already ON the roundabout (approaching from your right).

row.scene: Uncontrolled crossing (no signs, no robots) — a car comes from your RIGHT.
opts: Give way to the car on your right
row.ex: No signs? Yield to the vehicle on your RIGHT. 'Right goes first.'

row.scene: You are turning RIGHT across oncoming traffic. A car is coming straight from the opposite direction.
opts: Wait — the oncoming car going straight has priority
row.ex: Turning right = give way to oncoming traffic going straight. They have priority.

row.scene: An ambulance with flashing lights and a siren is behind you.
opts: Pull over to the LEFT and stop until it passes
Stop in the middle of the road
row.ex: Always give emergency vehicles right of way — pull over left and stop.

row.scene: Yield sign ahead, but the road looks completely clear.
opts: Slow down, check, and proceed if safe — no need for a full stop
row.ex: At a YIELD sign, you slow and give way if needed. If it's clear, you may proceed — you don't have to stop completely.

sources.signs: SADC official K53 syllabus + verified SVG assets
